battle.name: 蕭銑起事
battle.brief: 大業十三年（617）冬，梁宗之後蕭銑在吳郡起兵，據蘇州富庶之地置官收兵，翌年稱帝建吳，以城守與水軍斷糧相持數載。吳郡終為沈法興所奪，蕭銑退保會稽。卡面所示的斯巴達長矛，正與城守軍手中的自製竹木矛同源：削尖木桿加金屬矛頭，在城頭與水際抵住壓上來的敵手。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。

countries: 蕭銑起事爆發於隋大業十三年（617）冬，戰場在江南吳郡（今江蘇蘇州）一帶及其外圍的太湖水道，後轉入會稽（越州，今浙江紹興）。叛方是由梁武帝蕭衍之孫蕭銑所領、以吳郡豪右與郡兵為骨幹的割據政權：蕭銑憑宗室的名分起兵，據吳郡城之後置百官、收編州郡武備、徵發鄉里人丁，兵源以吳郡鄉里、郡兵、逃戶與亡命為主，編制鬆散，多屬臨時糾合的部曲與鄉兵，極少有可作野戰之用的整建部隊。官方一方是隋朝在江南的州郡體系：吳郡太守與郡丞以下仍各據城邑，郡兵、縣兵與徵發的鄉兵固守城牆與渡口，隋廷另派撫慰使與行軍將校居間調處，但隋煬帝本人遠在江都，政令屢斷，鞭長莫及。與蕭銑並起於江淮的還有沈法興、張善安等地方武人，三方在吳郡、會稽一帶互相攻併，一度形成隋方、蕭方、沈方角力的局面。最終平定蕭銑的是唐朝武裝，李勣、裴出士等將領率軍沿江南水道南下；唐朝接管之後，改以州兵、郡兵與團練的形式整編舊部，殘餘的起義武裝被拆散編入各州。
countriesEn: Xiao Xian's uprising broke out in the winter of Sui's Daye 13 (617). The theatre was Wu Commandery in Jiangnan, present-day Suzhou in Jiangsu, together with the waterways of Lake Tai, and the struggle later shifted to Kuaiji, Yuezhou, present-day Shaoxing in Zhejiang. The rebel side was a regional regime headed by Xiao Xian, a grandson of Emperor Wu of the Liang, and built on the magnates of Wu and on the commandery's own soldiers: taking advantage of his princely descent he rose in arms, and once he held the city he set up a full set of offices, took over the regional military stores and pressed local households into service. His strength came from local kin groups, commandery levies, absentees from the tax registers and men already in flight; the organisation was loose, built out of hastily gathered bands and village militia, and he had almost nothing that could be fielded as a battle line. The official side was the Sui administrative structure in Jiangnan: the governor and the lesser officers of Wu Commandery still held their walled towns, commandery and county levies and conscripted village militia defended the walls and the ferry crossings, and the court sent a handful of pacifying envoys and marching commanders to arbitrate, but Emperor Yang himself was far away at Jiangdu, decrees no longer crossed the river and the capital could not reach the south. Alongside Xiao Xian rose Shen Faxing and Zhang Shan'an, local strongmen of the Jianghuai region, and the three parties fought and absorbed one another around Wu and Kuaiji, producing a triangular contest between the Sui party, the Xiao party and the Shen party. The force that finally ended Xiao Xian's state was Tang's: generals such as Li Ji, formerly Xu Shiji, and Pei Chushi brought troops down the inland waterways. After the handover, Tang reorganised the old rebel bands into prefectural troops, commandery troops and local militia, breaking the old units up and distributing them among the prefectures.
people: 核心人物是蕭銑本人。史傳他出身梁宗，隋代曾在江南仕宦，熟悉吳郡的戶籍、倉場與水陸交通，起事時以吳郡本地豪族與郡吏為骨幹，一夜之間控制郡城與府庫。他最關鍵的決定是於武德元年（618）在吳郡稱帝，國號吳，年號太平，後遷都會稽，把江南最富庶的兩郡作為根本；這在隋末群雄中獨樹一幟，卻也讓他放棄了整合江南全局的機會。他的對手方面：沈法興同為吳郡人，先與蕭銑合起兵，後背叛並攻陷吳郡，奪其城邑；隋方將領張善安以撫慰使的身分在江淮周旋，曾與沈法興、蕭銑相持；宇文化及在江都弒隋煬帝，使江南失去中央的號令，蕭銑的政權正是在這個真空裡坐大。北方同時並起的李密、竇建德、杜伏威等人則各占地盤，與蕭銑互不相屬。唐方的主要人物是李勣（徐世勣），他於武德四年在黃浦一線擊破沈法興，間接終結了蕭銑的吳；裴出士則在武德五年於會稽擒獲蕭銑，將其檻送長安。蕭銑的部將姓名在傳世記載中多已散佚，只留下「大將數人、姓名不詳」的概況，這是這場戰爭記錄上最明顯的空缺。
peopleEn: The central figure is Xiao Xian himself. Tradition makes him a scion of the Liang imperial clan who had held office in Jiangnan under the Sui, and who knew the registers, the granaries and the water routes of Wu Commandery intimately; when he rose he leaned on the local magnates and on former commandery clerks, and took the city and its treasuries in a single night. His most consequential decision was to proclaim himself emperor at Wu in the first year of Wude (618), founding the state of Wu with the era name Taiping, and later to move the capital to Kuaiji, taking the two richest commanderies of Jiangnan as his base. That was unique among the contenders of the late Sui, and it also cost him the chance to unify Jiangnan. On the opposing side, Shen Faxing, also a native of Wu, first rose together with Xiao Xian and then betrayed him, taking Wu Commandery and its city. The Sui commander Zhang Shan'an moved about the Jianghuai region in the capacity of pacifying envoy and was stalemated in turn by Shen Faxing and by Xiao Xian. Yuwen Huaji murdered Emperor Yang at Jiangdu, which stripped Jiangnan of any central authority and allowed Xiao Xian's regime to grow in the resulting vacuum. Meanwhile Li Mi, Dou Jiande, Du Fuwei and others rose in the north, each holding ground of their own and belonging to no alliance with Xiao Xian. On the Tang side the principal names are Li Ji, formerly Xu Shiji, who broke Shen Faxing's line at Huangpu in the fourth year of Wude and so indirectly sealed the fate of Xiao Xian's Wu, and Pei Chushi, who captured him at Kuaiji in the fifth year of Wude and sent him in a cage to the Tang capital. The names of Xiao Xian's own commanders have largely perished from the record; all that survives is the bare statement that he had several generals whose names are unknown, and this is the most obvious lacuna in the documentation of the war.
kits: 卡面這件兵器是斯巴達長矛：兩米長的木桿，前端裝銅制矛頭，尾端套一截銅箍以加重並配重，重心偏後，原本配一面小圓盾使用。這種原始的希臘樣式從未出現在隋末江南的戰場上，但它的形制恰好是當時鄉民兵唯一做得起的樣板：削尖的竹桿與木桿、敲平的舊銅器、犁頭或破鍋片纏上麻繩，便成了一件完整的長矛，與斯巴達人手中的標槍在功能上完全一致。史書沒有留下蕭銑部眾用何種矛的記載，這一點可以確定；但同期隋唐戰役的旁證顯示，郡兵與義軍大量配用自製長矛，兵刃多為鐵矛頭安於長桿，無鐏而柄身不均，只在近身纏鬥中發揮作用；官軍的制式裝備則是隋制長矛與槊，槊更長更重，供武官與重裝騎兵使用。蕭銑據吳郡，還有一項別處沒有的資源：太湖與江南河的水網。隋末吳郡是江淮造船的中心，大業年間為第三次征高句麗在吳郡、京口一帶大造戰船，史載船數達二千餘艘，黃龍、五牙一類的船型與相應的船工、木料都留在本地，蕭銑的部眾因此得以用小艇與鬥艦控制湖面、封鎖渡口，而隋廷的江都水軍與後來唐軍的舟師在江南作戰，同樣要靠這一套船塢與船工。防禦方面是吳郡的城門、城牆、女牆與雉堞，配角弓、臂弓與強弩；攻城與野戰的器材則是撞竿、雲梯、攻城車、拒馬、鹿角與壕柵。糧秣由太湖、江南河與沿海的稻米、漁獲與漕運支應，吳郡是隋廷倚重的財賦之區，這是起義軍能據城自立、官軍也能就地取糧的共同前提。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Spartan dory: a wooden shaft some two metres long with a bronze head at the front and a bronze sleeve fitted to the butt as both weight and counterbalance, so that the balance point sits well back, and it was originally carried with a small round shield. This archaic Greek pattern never appeared on a battlefield in late Sui Jiangnan, but its construction was precisely the cheapest pattern the village levies of that time could copy: a sharpened bamboo or wooden shaft, a flattened old bronze fitting, a ploughshare or a piece of a smashed cauldron bound on with hemp cord, and the result is a complete spear, functionally identical to the sarissa in a Spartanman's hands. The histories do not record what kind of spear Xiao Xian's men used, and that much can be stated with certainty; but the parallel evidence from Sui and Tang battles of the same years shows that commandery troops and rebel bands were issued large quantities of home-made spears, their blades usually iron heads fitted to long shafts, without a socket ferrule and of uneven balance, useful chiefly in close fighting. The regular equipment of the government troops was the Sui-pattern spear together with the shao, a longer and heavier shafted weapon for officers and heavily armed cavalry. Holding Wu gave Xiao Xian a resource found nowhere else: the water network of Lake Tai and the Jiangnan Canal. In the last years of the Sui, Wu was the shipbuilding centre of the Jianghuai, and during the third campaign against Goguryeo the Sui built a great fleet at Wu and Jingkou, the number of hulls recorded reaching more than two thousand; hull types such as the Huanglong and the Wuya, together with the shipwrights and the timber, all remained on the spot. Xiao Xian's followers could therefore use light boats and fighting junks to control the lake and seal the crossings, and the Sui war fleet at Jiangdu, and later the Tang fleets operating in Jiangnan, depended on the same yards and the same shipwrights. On the defensive side were the gates, walls, parapets and crenellations of Wu city, furnished with horn bows, arm bows and strong crossbows; the siege and field equipment consisted of battering rams, scaling ladders, siege towers, cheval-de-frise, caltrops and palisades. Food and fodder came from the rice, the fishing and the transport traffic of Lake Tai, the Jiangnan Canal and the coast; Wu was one of the fiscal districts on which the Sui treasury relied, and that was the common premise which allowed the rebels to hold a city and the government troops to feed themselves on the spot.
tactics: 蕭銑的戰法由地理決定。吳郡是水鄉，腹地有太湖，東南通松江與浙東，西接建業、揚州，處在隋廷南北漕運與江淮物資的孔道之上。他起兵之後沒有選擇北進或西征，而是以吳郡城為核心做三件事：控制城門、府庫與渡口，收編郡兵與願附的鄉兵；在太湖與江南河上以小艇封鎖水道，斷絕隋方與沈法興的糧船與偵騎；再以郡兵與鄉隊分守沿線城邑與關津，遇敵大至則退保城池，不與敵決戰於開闊之地。這是典型的以城守與遊擊拖延的戰術：靠水斷糧、以城消耗，拖得越久，隋廷與唐廷越無法抽身。蕭銑的弱點也正在這套打法上——他始終沒有把水軍與步卒編成可以野戰的統一軍團，一旦吳郡城被合圍或水道被封死，部眾便各自潰散。與蕭銑對峙的一方，隋方將校與沈法興都以舟師沿江南河上溯或東下，逼近城郊再登岸列陣；唐軍更為嚴整，武德四年李勣在黃浦一線以水軍斷沈法興的退路，再以騎兵與步卒夾擊河道，江南的城邑逐個被奪回。唐軍對會稽的收官之作是裴出士的奇襲：傳稱他假意歸附，誘蕭銑出城交易，隨即以埋伏的甲士縛之，一戰而擒其首，全程沒有經過攻城戰。
tacticsEn: Xiao Xian's way of war was dictated by geography. Wu was a watery country: Lake Tai lay at its heart, the east ran through Songjiang towards eastern Zhejiang, the west towards Jianye and Yangzhou, and the whole district sat astride the Sui's north-south transport artery and the goods traffic of the Jianghuai. After raising his forces he chose neither to march north nor to campaign west. Instead he made the city of Wu his pivot and did three things: he took the gates, the treasury and the ferry landings, and folded in the commandery levies and the village bands willing to join him; he used light boats on Lake Tai and the Jiangnan Canal to seal the water routes and cut the grain junks and scouting parties of the Sui party and of Shen Faxing; and he garrisoned the towns and passes along his lines with commandery troops and village detachments, falling back into the walled cities whenever a main enemy force came up, and refusing to give battle in open ground. This was a delaying doctrine of city defence and harrying: cutting supply by water and wearing the enemy down behind walls, so that the longer it lasted the less the Sui court and the Tang court could disengage. The weakness lay in the same method, for Xiao Xian never fused his flotilla and his foot into a single force capable of open battle, and once the city of Wu was surrounded or the water routes closed, his bands dissolved piecemeal. Faced with him, the Sui commanders and Shen Faxing alike moved war-junks up the Jiangnan Canal or down it, closing on the suburbs before they landed and drew up in order; the Tang were stricter still, and in the fourth year of Wude Li Ji used his fleet to cut Shen Faxing's retreat at Huangpu and then caught him between cavalry and foot on the river line, taking the Jiangnan cities one by one. The closing move against Kuaiji was a coup by Pei Chushi: tradition has it that he pretended to submit, lured Xiao Xian out of his city to a parley, and had him bound by soldiers lying in wait, taking the rebel chief alive in a single stroke, with no siege of any kind.
data: 這場起事的可核數字相當稀少，以下只列可以確定的部分。時間上，起事在隋大業十三年（617）冬，月份諸說並存，通常繫於是年十一月；蕭銑稱帝建吳在武德元年（618）春，隋煬帝遇害於同年三月江都；吳郡失守、蕭銑退保會稽在武德二至三年（619至620）之間；唐軍在黃浦擊破沈法興是武德四年（621）秋後；蕭銑在會稽被擒是武德五年（622），其後在長安被誅。地理尺度上，吳郡至京口約三百里，至江都約五百里，至會稽約六百里，而京口與江都之間的江南河與太湖水道可以行駛大型戰船，這是當年各方爭奪的關鍵；由吳郡到長安則需二千數百里，隋廷的調兵與轉糧在關中與江南之間要走上數月。兵力方面，蕭銑的部眾人數史無明確記載，僅知吳郡豪右多有響應、郡兵多被收編；隋廷在江南的郡兵與縣兵分散各城，總數無從考訂；唐軍在江南的兵力以水軍與隨軍騎兵為主，數字亦無存錄。可以確定的是，隋自大業八年（612）第三次征高句麗之後連年用兵，役使與轉輸不絕，全國戶口銳減，江南的攤派與徭役尤重，這正是隋末江南先後出現吳郡、會稽、丹陽一帶割據的直接背景。
dataEn: The verifiable figures for this rising are scarce, and only what can be established is set down here. In time, the revolt began in the winter of Daye 13 (617); the month is given variously and is usually placed in November of that year. Xiao Xian proclaimed himself emperor and founded Wu in the spring of the first year of Wude (618), and Emperor Yang was murdered at Jiangdu in the third month of the same year. The loss of Wu Commandery and Xiao Xian's withdrawal to Kuaiji fall between the second and third years of Wude, 619 to 620. The Tang fleet broke Shen Faxing at Huangpu in the autumn of the fourth year of Wude (621), and Xiao Xian was captured at Kuaiji in the fifth year of Wude (622), after which he was executed at the Tang capital. In scale, Wu lies about three hundred li from Jingkou, about five hundred from Jiangdu and about six hundred from Kuaiji, and the Jiangnan Canal and the waters of Lake Tai between Jingkou and Jiangdu could carry large warships; that reach of water was the prize all parties fought over. From Wu to Chang'an is more than two thousand li, so Sui troops and Sui grain moving between the Guanzhong basin and Jiangnan took months on the road. On numbers of men, the record for Xiao Xian's following is silent: all that is known is that many Wu magnates answered the call and that commandery soldiers were taken over wholesale. The Sui commandery and county levies in Jiangnan were dispersed among separate towns and cannot be totalled, and the Tang force in Jiangnan consisted chiefly of river troops with attached cavalry, again without any figure preserved. What is certain is that the Sui went on campaigning year after year after the third expedition against Goguryeo in Daye 8 (612); the labour levies and the transport service never stopped, the registered households of the realm fell away, and the assessments and forced service laid on Jiangnan were heavier than anywhere else in the empire. That is the direct background to the succession of breakaway regimes at Wu, at Kuaiji and at Danyang in the last years of the Sui.
cause: 蕭銑起事有三重原因疊在一起。最外層是隋朝的崩解：大業年間三次征伐高句麗，役夫與轉輸的負擔壓在江南，煬帝又遷都江都，把江淮變成行宮與後庫，江都以南的州郡實際上與中央隔絕；及至武德元年（618）江都弒帝，江南的政令自此斷絕，各州郡的太守、縣令各自守城自保，全國出現了數十處並起的大小割據。中層是吳郡本身的處境：吳郡是江南財賦與漕運的中心，倉庫儲滿而役使繁重，士族與豪右對隋廷的攤派與徵發積怨已久，隋廷一旦無法派兵，豪族與郡吏便各自尋找出路，而郡兵久在本地，亦樂於擁立一位名分響亮的領袖。內層是蕭銑個人的宗室名分：他以梁武帝蕭衍之孫的身份起兵，在隋末群雄中是最正統的一個名號，復梁之說在江南豪族中自有市場，因此吳郡的鄉里與地方武人多願意響應。與李密、竇建德那種以流民為主的起義不同，蕭銑的起事幾乎沒有流民成份，靠的是城市的資源、郡兵的裝備與豪族的人脈；這使它起得很快，也使它缺少可以流動與補充的根基，一旦失去城市與倉場，便再無從重建。
causeEn: Three causes lie one upon another behind Xiao Xian's revolt. The outermost is the disintegration of the Sui: the three campaigns against Goguryeo during the Daye era placed the burden of forced labour and transport on Jiangnan, and the emperor moved the capital to Jiangdu, turning the Jianghuai into a travelling palace and a reserve treasury, so that the prefectures south of the Yangtze were in practice cut off from the centre. When the emperor was murdered at Jiangdu in the first year of Wude (618) the chain of command in Jiangnan broke for good, and every prefect and magistrate shut himself into his own city: dozens of breakaway regimes of every size sprang up across the realm. The middle cause is the condition of Wu itself. Wu was the fiscal and transport heart of Jiangnan, its granaries full and its labour service heavy, and the local clans and magnates had long chafed at Sui assessments and conscription. Once the court could no longer send troops to hold them, the magnates and the commandery clerks began to look for ways out, and the commandery soldiers, stationed there for years, were glad to rally behind a leader with a commanding name. The innermost cause is Xiao Xian's own descent: he rose in arms as a grandson of Emperor Wu of the Liang, and among the contenders of the late Sui he carried the most legitimate title of them all. The talk of restoring the Liang had its own market among the Jiangnan magnates, which is why so many local households and local warriors of Wu answered him. Unlike the risings of Li Mi or Dou Jiande, which were made up largely of refugees and vagrants, Xiao Xian's revolt drew almost none of that sort: it rested on the resources of a city, on the equipment of the commandery troops and on the connections of the great families. That made it rise quickly, and it also left it without a mobile base that could be replenished; once it lost the city and its granaries there was no way to rebuild it.
impact: 蕭銑起事在隋末亂局中的直接影響有兩層。對江南而言，它把吳郡與會稽兩郡推成割據的權力中心：蕭銑設官署、收賦役、置軍備，使江南在隋廷崩解之後有一段相對穩定的秩序，同時也使吳郡成為各方爭奪的目標，隋方、沈方與唐方先後把兵鋒指向此地，江南的城邑因此反覆易主。對蕭銑本人而言，稱帝建吳在名分上是一次冒險的躍升：他是隋末少數公開稱帝的割據者之一，國號吳、年號太平的政令在江南一度有效，但同時也把他置於眾矢之的，並且讓他放棄了與北方群雄逐鹿的可能，只能在江南守成。從長遠看，這場起事加速了江南的權力轉移：沈法興以吳郡為基地建號，隨後被唐軍在黃浦打敗；唐朝平定江南之後，對舊隋官員與地方豪右採取錄用與安撫的辦法，蕭銑政權留下的州縣建置、水利與漕運網絡多被沿用，吳郡與會稽在唐初成為江南財賦的重鎮。也因此，蕭銑雖是一個短命政權，卻是隋亡唐興之間江南一環的關鍵節點。
impactEn: The immediate effects of Xiao Xian's rising within the chaos of the late Sui worked in two ways. For Jiangnan it turned the two commanderies of Wu and Kuaiji into the seats of a regional power: Xiao Xian set up offices, collected taxes and service dues, and organised military stores, and for a time gave Jiangnan a measure of order after the collapse of the Sui. At the same time it made Wu a target: the Sui party, the Shen party and the Tang party all turned their arms towards the district in turn, and the cities of the south changed hands again and again. For Xiao Xian himself, the proclamation of the Wu state was a daring leap in status. He was one of the very few breakaway rulers in the late Sui who openly assumed the imperial title, and the ordinances of the state of Wu under the era name Taiping were for a while effective in the south; but it also made him the common target of every rival and closed off any possibility of his competing with the northern contenders for the empire. He could only hold what he had. In the longer term the rising hastened the transfer of power in Jiangnan: Shen Faxing built his own regime on the base of Wu commandery and was in turn defeated by the Tang at Huangpu. After Tang had settled the south, the old Sui officials and local magnates were taken into service or placated, and much of what Xiao Xian's regime had built in the way of prefectural and county administration, waterworks and transport survived into the new order. Wu and Kuaiji became fiscal pillars of the Tang south. Xiao Xian's state was short-lived, but it was the hinge of the Jiangnan sequence between the fall of the Sui and the establishment of the Tang.
result: 結果是起事成功而政權短命。大業十三年冬，蕭銑在吳郡舉兵，憑宗室名分、豪族支持與郡城之固，一度盡有吳郡與會稽，並在翌年稱帝，國號吳、年號太平，是隋末南方聲勢最盛的割據者。但他既未能整合江南的其他勢力，也沒有解決北來的唐軍與南下的沈法興兩面受敵的處境。619至620年間沈法興攻陷吳郡，蕭銑放棄經營已久的根本，退保會稽，倚浙東山地與海路自守；622年，裴出士在會稽設計將他擒獲，檻送長安，隨後被處死，其所建政權至此終結。蕭銑的部眾則被唐軍收編為州兵、郡兵與團練，散入江南各州，舊日的水軍與船塢也由官府接收，成為唐朝水軍與漕運的基礎。歷史上這場起事通常被視為隋末江南割據的高峰與終結：它證明隋廷在失去對江南的控制之後已無力恢復，而唐朝正是藉著平定吳郡、會稽一帶的割據，完成了對江南的接管，這也是唐朝立國之後最急需的一步。
resultEn: The outcome was a successful revolt and a short-lived state. In the winter of Daye 13 Xiao Xian raised his forces at Wu Commandery, and with a princely title, the backing of the magnates and the strength of the city walls he held Wu and Kuaiji for a time, proclaiming himself emperor the following year under the state of Wu and the era name Taiping, and for a while he was the most imposing of the breakaway powers in the south. But he never managed to absorb the other Jiangnan forces, and he never solved the problem of being pressed from two sides, by Tang troops coming from the north and by Shen Faxing coming up from the south. Between 619 and 620 Shen Faxing took Wu Commandery, and Xiao Xian gave up the base he had laboured to build, falling back to Kuaiji and holding himself behind the hills of eastern Zhejiang and the sea road. In 622 Pei Chushi contrived to take him at Kuaiji and sent him in a cage to the Tang capital, where he was put to death; the state he had founded ended with him. His followers were taken into Tang service as prefectural troops, commandery troops and local militia and scattered among the prefectures of the south, while the old flotilla and the shipyards fell to the government and became the basis of the Tang river fleet and of the imperial transport system. In the historical account this rising is usually treated as the high point and the end of the breakaway regimes in late Sui Jiangnan. It showed that the Sui court, having lost control of the south, had no strength left to recover it, and it was by putting down the regimes around Wu and Kuaiji that the Tang completed its seizure of Jiangnan, the most urgent step after the founding of the dynasty.
